title: Adult Shop Promotions: Check Eligibility and Exclusions Before Ordering
description: Review adult shop promotion terms, exclusions, minimums, and checkout changes so you can compare offers against the actual order total.
excerpt: A promotion is useful only if it applies to the items and delivery choice you want. Check the terms and final checkout summary before placing an order.
keyTakeaways: Read the promotion's eligibility, exclusions, and end conditions before adding items to a cart.
Check whether minimums, product categories, or account requirements affect the offer.
Compare the final checkout summary with the advertised terms before submitting an order.
Keep a private record of the offer and the final order total if the promotion is important to your decision.

sections.heading: Treat the offer as a set of conditions
paragraphs: A promotion headline is only a starting point. The terms may specify which products qualify, whether a minimum spend applies, whether the offer is limited to certain account holders, and whether it can be combined with another offer. Check these details before assuming that a product shown near the promotion qualifies. The conditions may appear on a promotion page, in a banner link, or during checkout, so follow the associated terms rather than relying on a short headline.

Make a short list of the conditions that could change your decision. For example, note any excluded categories, required code, minimum order value, or use-by date. If the terms do not explain how eligibility is determined, avoid building an order around an assumption. A promotion is not worth adding unnecessary items or changing a planned purchase if the final benefit is unclear.
bullets: Locate the full terms and note any eligibility conditions.
Check whether a code or account sign-in is required.
Identify exclusions and any stated time limits.
Do not add an unwanted item solely to meet a minimum.

sections.heading: Check the items, not just the cart value
paragraphs: A minimum spend does not necessarily mean every item contributes toward eligibility. Some offers can apply only to selected products or exclude sale items, bundles, or particular categories. Review the offer against the items in your cart one by one. If the shop provides a qualifying-products list, use that instead of assuming that the whole catalog is included.

Pay attention to bundle and variant details. A promotion might apply to one version but not another, or may exclude products already discounted. If a qualifying item changes to an unavailable option or a different variant, the offer may no longer apply. Before checkout, confirm that the item name, selected option, and promotion terms still match the order you intended.

sections.heading: Compare the final checkout with the offer
paragraphs: The cart and checkout summary are the point to verify whether an offer has been applied. Check the displayed line items, any promotion code, the order subtotal, delivery charges, taxes or other stated charges, and the total shown before submitting. A discount may affect only part of an order. Do not infer the final amount from the banner or from the value of items before delivery and other charges are included.

If the order summary differs from what you expected, stop before placing the order. Check for an ineligible product, a code that was not accepted, a minimum that was not met, or a rule preventing offers from combining. If the page does not explain the difference, contact the shop through its official support route before completing the purchase. Keep the inquiry factual and avoid sharing more personal information than needed to ask about the offer.
bullets: Confirm the offer appears in the final order summary.
Review the whole order total, including stated delivery and other charges.
Stop if the discount or eligibility is not clear.
Save a copy of the terms and summary if the offer affects your decision.

sections.heading: Watch for account and marketing conditions
paragraphs: Some offers may require an account, newsletter subscription, or other opt-in. Decide whether that condition is worth accepting before proceeding. A discount is a separate decision from whether you want marketing messages or an ongoing account. Review the relevant settings and the shop's explanation of how contact information will be used. If an opt-in is optional, do not select it automatically as part of the promotion process.

Consider the privacy of offer-related emails and notifications. If you share an inbox or device, promotional messages can reveal a retailer relationship through subject lines, previews, or order updates. Adjust notification settings and device previews according to your own privacy needs. Keep order records accessible to you, but avoid placing them in shared folders or calendars that disclose more than necessary.

sections.heading: Compare the offer with your original purchase plan
paragraphs: Promotions can encourage a larger or different order than intended. Compare the final cart with your original list: are the items still wanted, do the selected options still fit your needs, and are you comfortable with the full order total? If the offer requires extra spending or changes the delivery choice, evaluate those changes as part of the purchase rather than as a free bonus.

A useful test is to compare two versions of the order: the items you planned to buy without the offer and the cart required to qualify. Consider the complete total and whether the added items are genuinely useful. If the promotional cart is less suitable, ordering without the offer or not ordering may be the better fit. The purpose of checking eligibility is to make the offer legible, not to maximize discount use.

sections.heading: Keep a clear record without oversharing
paragraphs: If you decide to use a promotion, keep the terms, code, and final summary in a private record. A dated screenshot can be useful if the offer is important, but check that it does not capture unrelated personal details, payment information, or private browser tabs. Keep the order confirmation with the same record so you can compare what was advertised with what was charged.

If the offer does not apply after checkout, review the receipt and the terms before contacting support. Include the order reference and a concise explanation, but avoid sending unnecessary payment details. Use the shop's official contact route and retain the response. A clear record does not guarantee a particular resolution, but it can help identify whether the discrepancy came from eligibility, an excluded item, or a checkout display.

faqs.question: Should I add items to reach a promotion minimum?
faqs.answer: Only if you actually want the added items and the complete order still makes sense. Check which products count toward the minimum and compare the full order total with your original purchase plan.

faqs.question: Why might an advertised offer not appear in my cart?
faqs.answer: Possible reasons include an excluded item, a minimum that was not met, an unaccepted code, an account condition, or a rule about combining offers. Check the terms and checkout summary before submitting the order.

faqs.question: Does a discount apply to delivery or other charges?
faqs.answer: That depends on the offer terms. Review the itemized summary and do not assume a promotion affects charges beyond the products it identifies.

faqs.question: What should I save if a promotion affects my decision?
faqs.answer: Keep the offer terms, any code or eligibility note, the final checkout summary, and the order confirmation in a private place. Avoid capturing payment details or unrelated personal information.
